scope.document_environment: Rendered preview of the current official-style PDF, not the final attached delivery.
scope.method: Actual visual inspection of the five PNG files using view_image; findings are not inferred only from extracted text.
scope.limits: Preview-image review assesses visible text/formula/citation layout, not a new numerical or bibliographic verification. The only initially suspected overflow was resolved through same-image raster bounds and root-provided PDFium glyph bounds.

document.pdf_format_as_recorded: Official NeurIPS 2025 style with a course notice

findings: Title, author/ID and Unconstrained Optimization direction are legible.
Abstract explicitly scopes 73/90 to the recorded Windows reference run; 26/90 and the other preserved counts are readable.
Introduction citations [7, 8] and the single concise code-attachment entry are readable; no overlap or clipping is visible.
Literature text, the comparison table, and citations [1]–[7] are legible within the text block.
Strong-convexity assumptions for the cited BFGS rates and the distinction between modified L-BFGS and tested full-memory BFGS are visible.
No formula, table, or body-text clipping is visible.
Equations (1)–(4), sum limits, superscripts and the analytic Rastrigin gradient are legible.
The Rosenbrock nonconvexity example distinguishes a nonstationary indefinite-Hessian point from a saddle point.
Gradient-check tolerances and the local-conditioning qualification are readable. The GD subsection fits above the footer without overlap.
73/90 is explicitly identified as the recorded Windows reference result.
Platform limits state that pinned NumPy/SciPy do not guarantee identical floating-point paths and that near-threshold classifications may vary.
The page does not state a Linux outcome count or assign a definite numerical-library cause.
Historical Windows-to-Windows comparisons are distinguished from this revision’s unit tests and read-only checks, with no claim of a new formal experiment or cross-platform identity.
Discussion, reproducibility paragraph and conclusion are legible and do not overlap.
All eight references and the two version-specific SciPy documentation links are readable.
The final note describes the official PDF style and contains no Word-version statement.
Reference [7]’s GitHub URL fits within the common right text edge; the initial apparent-overrun observation was disproved on recheck of the identical image.
